text:
maya: Heads-up — ran a prod-scale load test with OpenTelemetry spans fully ON. Observed p99 API latency +20-30% and api-frontend CPU ~2x. Attaching quick metrics dump and a couple traces.

kevin: Can you paste span counts and exporter config? My gut says exporter sync/serialization is stealing cycles.

maya: Spans/request ~45 (DB, cache, router, model-infer, kv-cache ops included). Exporter: OTLP/gRPC -> telemetry-cluster, batch_size=32, batch_timeout_ms=2000, sampling=100% for the test. No compression.

olga: 45 is higher than I expected. Are we creating fine-grained subspans inside model infer loop? Any retries creating duplicate spans? Can you share pprof or flame?

maya: Quick prometheus snapshot: 
otel_spans_received_total=1.2e6
otel_spans_exported_total=1.15e6
otel_exporter_send_duration_seconds_p50=0.003
otel_exporter_send_duration_seconds_p99=0.18
api_frontend_cpu_seconds_total (per pod) rose from ~1200 -> ~2400 during run.

sam: Two immediate hypotheses: (1) serialization + gRPC framing CPU for millions of spans; (2) exporter flush threads blocking application workers during GC/lock contention. Did you try increasing batch_size or async exporter?

maya: I tried batch_size=128 + batch_timeout_ms=5000 -> exporter p99 latency rose a bit but CPU dropped ~30% and api p99 improved (still ~+10% vs no-traces). Memory footprint increased because buffers hold more spans.

kevin: Good. Also worth experimenting with sampling at the edge: head-based 10% + keep-on-error. That should cut volume drastically while preserving error signals.

olga: Agree on sampling. For rollout metrics we need high fidelity on errors/latency spikes. Consider tail-sampling rules: keep all spans with status!=OK, sample others. That avoids losing rare failures.

maya: Ran tail-sampling prototype: keep-if-error else 10% sample. Result: span volume down ~72%, exporter CPU back near baseline, api p99 within ~2% of no-spans. Still need longer runs but looks promising.

infra-bot: deploy-bot: created experiment telemetry/edge-sample-10-batch-128 (variant id: telem-exp-2026-02-xx)

sam: Next experiments to try: switch exporter serialization to proto vs JSON (proto should be smaller/faster), try OTLP/HTTP + gzip to see CPU vs network tradeoff, and test increasing exporter worker pool. Also check if we can avoid creating spans for hot internal RPCs that add little signal.

kevin: Can someone add a dashboard panel correlating otel_spans_received (rate), exporter_send_latency_p99, cpu_per_pod, and request_p99. Add annotations for when batch_size/sampling changed so we can correlate.

maya: Added a dashboard and a short test plan to the internal note: https://redwood.internal/notes/telemetry-overhead. Plan: 24h runs for each config, capture p99, CPU, heap, exporter p99, and trace completeness for errors. TL;DR: batching + tail-sampling gets us inside SLO margins at acceptable retention cost.

olga: Nice work. One follow-up: file a tiny RFC on retention/analysis bias. Sampling reduces storage but will skew any post-hoc analytics that expect full signal. We'll need clear docs and defaults. Let's put this on Wed sync agenda.

maya: Will do. Thanks team :thumbsup:
